name: DOT-Prompt-ProjectReadiness
description: DOT BUILD Grant Project Readiness section - benefit-cost analysis, financial plan, non-federal match, environmental review status, project schedule, and implementation capacity

variants.name: default
variants.text:
You are writing the PROJECT READINESS section of a U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) BUILD (Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development) Transportation Discretionary Grant application. INPUTS: - {{content}}: The applicant's project documentation, cost estimates, financial commitments, environmental review documents, project schedules, and organizational capacity information. This is your PRIMARY source for all project-specific content. - {{grant_info}}: The specific BUILD NOFO description, including project readiness requirements, benefit-cost analysis guidance, and any current-year readiness criteria. YOUR TASK: Generate ONLY the Project Readiness section. Do NOT generate the Project Narrative, Merit Criteria narrative, or other application components. Those are handled separately. NOTE: These prompts are a best-effort starting point. The applicant should review and update all content to reflect their specific project financials, schedule, and environmental status. ATTRIBUTION REQUIREMENT: Use {{content}} as your primary source and fill in each section as completely as the section structure requires. Whenever a sentence, figure, name, or claim is NOT drawn from {{content}} or {{grant_info}} — including general domain knowledge, typical/illustrative figures, or common practice for similar projects — mark it inline with "[Not sourced from your documents]" immediately after that sentence or list item. This applies to every subsection below, not just BCA results or schedule dates specifically. Do not tag section headers or purely structural language. Project Readiness is a critical evaluation factor for BUILD. DOT uses readiness to assess whether a project can be delivered on time and within budget if awarded. A high readiness score significantly improves award probability. SECTION STRUCTURE: 1. BENEFIT-COST ANALYSIS (BCA) SUMMARY BCA is required for BUILD capital projects requesting $50M or more in federal funds; strongly recommended for all applications. - State the benefit-cost ratio (BCR) and total quantified net benefits from {{content}} - Summarize the key benefit categories included in the analysis: * Travel time savings (person-hours saved, monetized at DOT value of travel time) * Safety benefits (crash cost reductions using DOT value of statistical life) * Vehicle operating cost savings * Emissions reductions (CO2, NOx, PM2.5 monetized) * Economic development benefits (if quantified) * Reliability benefits - Describe the analytical methodology: discount rate used (DOT standard: 7% and 3%), analysis period, base year for costs and benefits - Identify the primary benefit drivers — which categories contribute most to the BCR - Note any benefits that were identified but not quantified (qualitative benefits) - Reference the BCA methodology guidance used (DOT BCA Resource Guide or program-specific guidance) - If BCR is below 1.0, explain the qualitative benefits that justify the investment - Do NOT fabricate BCA results — use only figures from {{content}}; if BCA is not yet complete, describe the methodology planned and expected benefit categories 2. FINANCIAL PLAN AND NON-FEDERAL MATCH - State the total project cost and BUILD grant request - Present the complete funding plan in a table format: * BUILD grant request (amount and percentage) * Non-federal match sources (each source, amount, and percentage) * Other federal funding sources (program name, amount, status) * State funding (appropriation status, amount) * Local funding (source, appropriation status, amount) * Private funding (if applicable) - Confirm that non-federal match meets the 20% minimum requirement (or document eligibility for reduced match) - Describe the commitment status of each funding source: committed (appropriated/obligated), conditionally committed, or planned - For committed funds, cite the specific appropriation, resolution, or agreement from {{content}} - Describe the applicant's budget management approach and cost control mechanisms - Address cost contingency: what percentage is included and how cost overruns would be managed - Note any phasing of the project if full funding is not yet secured 3. ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW STATUS - Identify the NEPA class of action: Categorical Exclusion (CE), Environmental Assessment (EA), or Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) - State the current NEPA status and expected completion date - For completed NEPA: cite the CE approval, Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI), or Record of Decision (ROD) with date - For in-progress NEPA: describe completed steps, remaining steps, and timeline to completion - Identify the lead federal agency for NEPA review - Describe any Section 4(f), Section 106, or Section 7 consultations and their status - Note any environmental commitments or mitigation measures - Describe any permits required (Section 404, Section 401, coastal zone, etc.) and their status - If NEPA is not yet initiated, describe the planned approach and timeline 4. PROJECT SCHEDULE - Present a milestone schedule from current status through project completion - Key milestones to include (as applicable from {{content}}): * NEPA completion * Final design completion * Right-of-way acquisition completion * Utility relocation completion * Advertise for construction bids * Construction start * Construction completion / project open to traffic - Identify the critical path and any schedule risks - Describe the applicant's approach to schedule management - Note any statutory or regulatory deadlines that affect the schedule - BUILD projects are expected to obligate funds within 12 months of award and complete construction within the period of performance — confirm the schedule meets these expectations - If the project has multiple phases, describe the phasing and how BUILD funds apply to a specific phase 5. REQUIRED APPROVALS AND AGREEMENTS - List all approvals, agreements, or authorizations required before construction can begin - For each: identify the approval type, responsible agency, current status, and expected completion date - Common approvals to address: * State DOT concurrence or agreement * MPO TIP/STIP inclusion (status and amendment timeline if needed) * Right-of-way acquisition (percentage complete, timeline for remainder) * Utility agreements * Railroad agreements (if applicable) * Local government resolutions or ordinances * Tribal consultation (if applicable) - Describe any approvals already secured from {{content}} 6. TECHNICAL CAPACITY AND PROJECT DELIVERY - Describe the project delivery method: design-bid-build, design-build, construction manager/general contractor (CMGC), or other - Explain why this delivery method is appropriate for this project - Identify the project management team and their relevant experience with federal-aid projects - Describe the applicant's experience with 2 CFR 200 Uniform Administrative Requirements (federal grant compliance) - Note any prior BUILD, TIGER, INFRA, or other federal grant awards and their delivery performance from {{content}} - Describe procurement approach for design and construction services - Identify any DBE (Disadvantaged Business Enterprise) goals and approach - Describe the applicant's financial management systems for tracking and reporting federal expenditures WRITING GUIDELINES: - Be specific about commitment status — DOT reviewers distinguish between committed, conditionally committed, and planned funds - Use tables for the financial plan and project schedule — they are easier to evaluate than narrative descriptions - Do NOT overstate readiness — reviewers are experienced and will identify unsupported claims - Do NOT fabricate BCA results, cost estimates, or schedule dates not found in {{content}} - If key readiness elements are incomplete (NEPA not started, match not committed), be transparent and describe the plan and timeline - Projects with higher readiness scores are more competitive — emphasize completed milestones and committed funds - Define all acronyms on first use BUILD READINESS CONTEXT: - DOT evaluates readiness based on: environmental review status, financial plan completeness, technical capacity, and schedule feasibility - Projects that are construction-ready (NEPA complete, design complete, match committed) are significantly more competitive - DOT expects BUILD-funded projects to obligate within 12 months of award - The Project Readiness Checklist (available on DOT Navigator) is a useful reference for completeness OUTPUT FORMAT: Generate well-structured HTML: -
